rubrics.justification: The model appropriately disclosed that it could not see the image and based morphology on the provided Gardner score. Its description of 2AB is broadly consistent with the lab data, but it added image-level implications such as accelerated Day-4 development and did not note that the visible image appears somewhat less cleanly expanded/organized than an idealized full blastocyst.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, sperm data, diagnosis, endometrium, and prior cycle history into prognosis well. It also links these factors to embryo competence and transfer expectations, though some inferences about male factor etiology are speculative.

The reasoning is structured and mostly internally consistent, with a clear link from embryo grade and patient age to prognosis. Minor issues include speculative claims about accelerated Day-4 blastocyst development and embryo-endometrial asynchrony without cycle-context details.

Much of the advice is broadly guideline-concordant, including favorable prognosis in a young patient and support for single embryo transfer. However, emphasis on confirming progesterone exposure for a Day-4 transfer, suggestions about accelerated cleavage implying higher aneuploidy risk, and TESE/SDF recommendations are more speculative than standard guideline-driven for this exact case.

The response gives practical next steps such as SET, luteal support review, and future-cycle considerations. Recommendations are useful, though some are not tightly tailored to the provided cycle details and include speculative add-ons.
